details:
Martian Map | Project Details

1. Project Overview

Martian Map is an interactive terrain analysis and intelligent route-planning platform developed by Orun Systems for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project focuses on Jezero Crater, Mars, and transforms real NASA/USGS-sourced Martian terrain data into an interactive 3D exploration environment.

The central challenge is that the shortest path between two locations is not necessarily the most suitable route for exploration. Steep slopes, elevation changes, irregular terrain, and scientific observation objectives must also be considered.

Martian Map addresses this challenge by integrating geospatial terrain analysis, slope-aware route planning, scientific waypoints, and astronaut mission simulation into a unified platform.

2. How Our System Works

Terrain Data Processing

The system uses Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data to represent Martian surface elevations. Terrain slope is calculated from elevation data, allowing the platform to analyze topographic conditions across a 1 km² study area in Jezero Crater.

Users can interactively inspect surface elevation, slope, and geographic coordinates at selected locations. Regional statistics include mean, median, maximum, and 95th-percentile slope values, supported by slope distribution visualizations.

Intelligent Route Planning

Martian Map uses the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate terrain-aware routes.

Instead of optimizing distance alone, the algorithm incorporates terrain slope into route costs and supports configurable slope constraints.

The platform also enables comparisons between distance-focused and slope-aware routes, helping users understand the trade-offs between route length and terrain difficulty.

Scientific Exploration Missions

Three scientific observation waypoints, evaluated using geological and topographic information, are integrated into the exploration environment.

The system calculates a mission route connecting these locations in sequence while considering terrain constraints.

Interactive Astronaut Simulation

An animated astronaut follows the planned route across the 3D Martian terrain.

The simulation includes multiple camera perspectives, movement telemetry, route progress tracking, and automatic waypoint status updates as destinations are reached.

This allows users to visualize the planned exploration mission rather than relying exclusively on static maps.

3. Technical Validation and Results

We evaluated our terrain processing and route-planning methods using quantitative validation.

  • The study area covers approximately 1 km² of Jezero Crater.
  • Elevation values at 25 sampled DEM points were verified against the source data.
  • One million slope pixels were consistently reproduced using the same calculation method.
  • A reference route generated under a 20° slope constraint measured 830 meters, with a maximum route-cell slope of 19.24°.
  • A separate scientific mission route connecting three observation waypoints measured approximately 1,360 meters, with an experimental 25° slope limit and a maximum modeled slope of 21.6°.

These results demonstrate the implementation and consistency of our terrain analysis and slope-constrained route-planning approach within the evaluated scenarios.

The selected slope limits are experimental planning parameters, not universal guarantees of safe astronaut or rover traversal.

4. Technologies and Data Sources

Martian Map combines several technologies and scientific data-processing methods:

  • React and TypeScript for the interactive web application.
  • Python for geospatial data processing and terrain analysis.
  • A* pathfinding for terrain-aware route calculation.
  • Digital Elevation Models (DEM) for elevation and slope analysis.
  • GDAL and GeoPackage for geospatial data processing and management.
  • Mars Equirectangular Projection (EQC) for Martian spatial data representation.
  • Interactive 3D visualization and animation for mission simulation.

Our scientific and visual resources include NASA/JPL-Caltech Mars 2020 imagery, USGS Astrogeology terrain and geological datasets, and Jezero Crater maps and panoramas from Freie Universität Berlin.

5. Innovation and Creativity

Martian Map brings terrain analysis, intelligent route planning, scientific exploration objectives, and immersive mission visualization together in a single interactive environment.

Rather than presenting Martian terrain as a static map, our platform allows users to investigate terrain conditions, compare routes, explore scientific destinations, and observe mission progress through an animated astronaut simulation.

The combination of scientific data and interactive visualization makes complex planetary terrain information more accessible and engaging.

6. Intended Impact and Future Potential

Martian Map is a research-oriented demonstration of how terrain-aware planning can support planetary exploration.

The platform provides an accessible environment for understanding the relationship between terrain conditions, route selection, and scientific mission objectives.

Future development could incorporate additional terrain hazards, rover-specific mobility models, energy consumption estimates, and more extensive mission-planning constraints.

Our vision is to bridge the gap between planetary data and exploration decisions.

We don't just map Mars. We plan its exploration.
